text:
alejandro: Heads up — product is planning a 6h ‘flash drop’ on Nov 27 (US prime). Traffic shape: lots of short requests, bursts up to 8x baseline for ~10-20m windows every 30m. We need a plan for GPU capacity, fallback model variants, and prewarm.
kim: Numbers? how many extra GPU hours are we talking?
alejandro: Rough back-of-envelope: baseline for that window is ~1.2k GPU-hours. If bursts hit 8x and we don’t mitigate, peak increment could be ~6-7k GPU-hours across the 6h window (very spiky). But with thin-pooling + quantized fallbacks we can probably cut that to ~1.5-2k extra.
jasper: Agree — thin pooling + prefix/KV cache reuse helps a lot for short queries. Also recommend short-lived reserved lanes for 10% of traffic (hot path) so tail latency stays low.
meera: For fallbacks I can bake a q4f16 variant with validation on prompt set. Latency tradeoff: q4f16 is ~1.6x faster on T4/RTX than fp16 and ~50% lower memory.
lin: APAC region has limited spare P100/T4 capacity on that day (marketplace quotas). If we offload part of burst to US region we need routing rules and a cross-region cache warm strategy.
alejandro: Proposed multi-pronged strategy:
- reserve a small dedicated pool (20% of forecast peak) for hot path
- enable autoscaler + thin-pooling for shared pool
- deploy quantized fallback model variant with canary
- warm KV/prefix caches during low-traffic hours
- plumb routing rules to failover APAC->US for non-sensitive traffic
kim: How do we config the autoscaler? can we express min/max in yaml?
jasper: Example autoscaler snippet (will push to repo):
```
autoscaler:
  name: flash-drop-2027
  min_replicas: 10   # dedicated reserved lanes
  max_replicas: 150  # cap to control spend
  scale_policy:
    cpu_target: 60
    token_throughput_target: 12000
    cooldown_s: 60
  thin_pool: true
  thin_pool_size_ratio: 0.6
```
meera: For model promotion: I'll run evals against the Canary prompt set today. If q4f16 BLEU/regression < 1% vs fp16, we can enable automatic fallback.
ops-bot: Reminder: quota thresholds for us-west1 GPUs will be locked at 80% on 2027-11-27 between 07:00-15:00 UTC per marketplace rules.
lin: That quota lock is the crux — we need to ensure our routing policy can divert to eu-west and us-east gracefully. Also verify network hop latency for KV cache miss tolerances.
alejandro: Cost tradeoffs: reserving dedicated capacity (~20% of peak) adds predictable commit cost but saves cold-start / rebatching overhead. If we rely solely on burst autoscaling we risk spiky on-demand costs and higher tail latency.
kim: Any micro-optimizations we can do to reduce GPU time? e.g., batch window tuning or short-circuiting small requests to smaller models.
jasper: Yes — implement request size gates: short requests (<128 tokens) go to a smaller 3B quantized model; medium to q4f16 7B; long to primary 13B fp16. That reduces avg tokens-per-GPU-hour.
meera: I’ll prepare the model matrix and perf table by EOD. Want to flag: we need regression alerts in Redwood Console for quality; set thresholds for top-n prompt sets.
alejandro: Ops runbook items:
- [alejandro] open a capacity commit PR for dedicated lanes (deadline: 48h)
- [meera] push q4f16 canary and perf table (deadline: 24h)
- [jasper] update autoscaler config + stress sim in staging (deadline: 24h)
- [lin] verify cross-region routing and latency (deadline: 36h)
- [kim] cost estimate and commit recommendation (deadline: 24h)
ops-bot: Created incident ticket INF-2027-081 and scheduled a 30m dry-run in staging tomorrow 02:00 UTC.
kim: One more ask — make sure the console shows token-level cost O(1min) granularity for the window so product can decide throttles in near real-time.
alejandro: Good call. Also add a fallback policy: if avg P95 latency > 650ms for >5m, switch 30% of heavy requests to cached summary responses and lower-quality model.
meera: Will also add a synthetic workload to warm KV caches starting 2h before drop.
lin: For APAC->US fallback, confirm GDPR/data routing rules — only non-PII traffic. Product will mark routes.
jasper: After dry-run, we should capture GPU-hours delta and compare against our cost model. If thin-pooling saves >30% GPU-hours we keep it on for future drops.
alejandro: Sounds good. We’ll reconvene after the dry-run. :thumbsup:
kim: Thanks team. I’ll start the cost spreadsheet now. :spiral_calendar:
